entries.name: Sequential Thinking
entries.what: One tool that lets an agent write down and revise its reasoning step by step. It touches nothing outside itself.
entries.licence: MIT (repository: Apache-2.0 for new contributions, MIT for older code)

manual: In the app it is on by default for every agent on Claude Code.
Needs Node, for npx.
By hand in Claude Code: claude mcp add sequential-thinking -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking
By hand in Codex: codex mcp add sequential-thinking -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking

entries.name: Time
entries.what: Gives the current time in a time zone and converts a time between time zones.
entries.licence: MIT (repository: Apache-2.0 for new contributions, MIT for older code)

manual: In the app it is on by default for every agent on Claude Code.
Needs uv, for uvx.
By hand in Claude Code: claude mcp add time -- uvx mcp-server-time
By hand in Codex: codex mcp add time -- uvx mcp-server-time

entries.name: Fetch
entries.what: Fetches a web address and returns the page as markdown. One tool. Its maker warns that it can reach local and internal addresses.
entries.licence: MIT (repository: Apache-2.0 for new contributions, MIT for older code)

manual: In the app it is on by default for every agent on Claude Code.
Needs uv, for uvx.
By hand in Claude Code: claude mcp add fetch -- uvx mcp-server-fetch
By hand in Codex: codex mcp add fetch -- uvx mcp-server-fetch
It obeys robots.txt for requests a model makes unless started with --ignore-robots-txt

entries.name: Filesystem
entries.what: Reads, writes, edits, moves and searches files inside the folders it is allowed. Under Claude Code those are the launch folder and every additional working directory, whatever folder the command names.
entries.licence: MIT (repository: Apache-2.0 for new contributions, MIT for older code)
entries.riskNote: Its maker marks write_file, edit_file and move_file as destructive: they overwrite or remove what was there.

manual: In the app it is off until you switch it on. It was on by default before 0.5.6.
Needs Node, for npx.
By hand in Claude Code: claude mcp add filesystem -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /path/to/allowed/folder
By hand in Codex: codex mcp add filesystem -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /path/to/allowed/folder
A client that supports roots replaces the folders on the command line with its own. Claude Code sends the launch folder and every added working directory.

entries.name: Git
entries.what: Reads status, diffs, history and branches of a local Git repository, and can stage, commit, reset the index, create a branch and check one out. Twelve tools, no push. It works on the whole repository that holds the folder it is given.
entries.licence: MIT (repository: Apache-2.0 for new contributions, MIT for older code)

manual: In the app it is off until you switch it on. It was on by default before 0.5.6.
Needs uv, for uvx.
By hand in Claude Code: claude mcp add git -- uvx mcp-server-git --repository path/to/git/repo
By hand in Codex: codex mcp add git -- uvx mcp-server-git --repository path/to/git/repo
The server walks up from that path to the top of the repository and allows calls anywhere inside it.

entries.name: GitHub MCP Server
entries.what: GitHub's own server: repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, code security, gists and notifications. Its tools include delete_file and delete_repository. A read only switch and tool groups narrow it.

manual: Needs Docker, installed and running.
Make a GitHub personal access token with only the permissions you want an agent to have, and set it as GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN.
By hand in Claude Code: claude mcp add github -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=$GITHUB_PAT -- docker run -i --rm -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server
Read only: add -e GITHUB_READ_ONLY=1 to the docker line.
GitHub also hosts the server at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ with the token sent as a header. Its install guides give the line for each client.
Codex, hosted: codex mcp add github --url https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ --bearer-token-env-var GITHUB_PAT_TOKEN

entries.name: Context7
entries.what: Looks up current documentation and code examples for a library, so an agent does not answer from memory. Two tools: find the library, then query its docs.

manual: In the app it is on by default for every agent on Claude Code, as the local package.
Needs Node, for npx.
By hand in Claude Code: claude mcp add --scope user context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp
By hand in Codex: codex mcp add context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp
A free API key from context7.com/dashboard raises the rate limits. Pass it with --api-key.
The maker also hosts it at https://mcp.context7.com/mcp and now points new setups there. Its own setup command is npx ctx7 setup

entries.name: MCP Toolbox for Databases
entries.what: Google's database server with ready made tool sets for many engines. The app starts the PostgreSQL set: one tool runs any SQL, the rest list tables, views, indexes, locks, settings and statistics.

manual: Needs Node, for npx, and a PostgreSQL database you can reach.
Set POSTGRES_DATABASE, POSTGRES_USER and POSTGRES_PASSWORD. POSTGRES_HOST defaults to localhost and POSTGRES_PORT to 5432.
By hand: add a server to your client with the command npx and the arguments -y @toolbox-sdk/server --prebuilt=postgres --stdio
In Claude Code that is: claude mcp add toolbox-postgres -- npx -y @toolbox-sdk/server --prebuilt=postgres --stdio
For another database swap postgres for its name. The README lists them.
Give the database user only the rights you want an agent to have: one tool runs any SQL.

entries.name: DBHub
entries.what: A small database server for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle and SQLite. Two tools by default: run SQL and search the schema. It has a read only mode, row limits and a query timeout.

manual: Needs Node 22.5 or later.
Set DSN to the connection string of the one database it should reach. The format is on the DBHub command line page.
By hand in Claude Code: claude mcp add --scope user dbhub -- npx @bytebase/dbhub@latest --transport stdio
DBHub reads the connection string from the --dsn flag first, then from DSN.
Give the database user only the rights you want an agent to have: execute_sql runs any SQL.

entries.name: Gmail MCP server
entries.what: Google's hosted Gmail server: searches and reads threads, creates drafts and adds or removes labels. Google lists ten tools and no send tool. Part of the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program.

manual: Join the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program and have a Google Cloud project.
In that project turn on the product API and its MCP API (gmailmcp.googleapis.com).
Set up the OAuth consent screen with the scopes Google lists for the product.
Create an OAuth client of type Web application, tick "Use this client for an AI-powered agent", and keep its client ID and client secret.
Server address: https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1 over streamable HTTP. Sign in is OAuth with your own client.
Antigravity: add the server with that address, client ID and client secret to ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json, then authenticate it from the /mcp panel.
Claude.ai and Claude Desktop: Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector. The redirect address on your OAuth client is https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback
Google's page gives no command for Claude Code or Codex, so there is no install button.

entries.name: Google Calendar MCP server
entries.what: Google's hosted Calendar server: lists calendars and events, creates, updates and deletes events, answers invitations and suggests meeting times. Nine tools. Part of the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program.

manual: Join the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program and have a Google Cloud project.
In that project turn on the product API and its MCP API (calendarmcp.googleapis.com).
Set up the OAuth consent screen with the scopes Google lists for the product.
Create an OAuth client of type Web application, tick "Use this client for an AI-powered agent", and keep its client ID and client secret.
Server address: https://calendarmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1 over streamable HTTP. Sign in is OAuth with your own client.
Antigravity: add the server with that address, client ID and client secret to ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json, then authenticate it from the /mcp panel.
Claude.ai and Claude Desktop: Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector. The redirect address on your OAuth client is https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback
Google's page gives no command for Claude Code or Codex, so there is no install button.

entries.name: Google Drive MCP server
entries.what: Google's hosted Drive server: searches, reads and downloads files, reads file details and permissions, and creates or copies files. Google lists eight tools and no delete tool. Part of the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program.

manual: Join the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program and have a Google Cloud project.
In that project turn on the product API and its MCP API (drivemcp.googleapis.com).
Set up the OAuth consent screen with the scopes Google lists for the product.
Create an OAuth client of type Web application, tick "Use this client for an AI-powered agent", and keep its client ID and client secret.
Server address: https://drivemcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1 over streamable HTTP. Sign in is OAuth with your own client.
Antigravity: add the server with that address, client ID and client secret to ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json, then authenticate it from the /mcp panel.
Claude.ai and Claude Desktop: Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector. The redirect address on your OAuth client is https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback
Google's page gives no command for Claude Code or Codex, so there is no install button.

entries.name: Exa
entries.what: Web search and page reading, hosted by Exa. Two tools by default, with an advanced search tool and an agent run tool that can be switched on.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http exa --scope user https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp
Or the maker's plugin, which adds two skills as well: claude plugin install exa@claude-plugins-official
Codex: codex mcp add exa --url https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp
It works with no sign in, at lower limits. Signing in to Exa, or an Exa API key, lifts them and unlocks Exa Agent.

entries.name: Brave Search
entries.what: Web, local, place, image, video and news search plus a summariser, through the Brave Search API. Every tool is a search.

manual: Needs Node, for npx.
Get a Brave Search API key and set it as BRAVE_API_KEY.
By hand: add a server to your client with the command npx and the arguments -y @brave/brave-search-mcp-server --transport stdio
In Claude Code that is: claude mcp add brave-search -- npx -y @brave/brave-search-mcp-server --transport stdio

entries.name: Firecrawl
entries.what: Scrapes, crawls, maps and searches the web, drives pages by clicking and typing, and runs scheduled page monitors that can alert by webhook or email. Calls draw Firecrawl credits.

manual: Needs Node 22 or later.
Get a Firecrawl API key and set it as FIRECRAWL_API_KEY. Never put the key in a server address or in a chat.
By hand: add a server to your client with the command npx and the arguments -y firecrawl-mcp
In Claude Code that is: claude mcp add firecrawl -- npx -y firecrawl-mcp
Firecrawl also hosts it at https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp with the key sent as a bearer header.

entries.name: Playwright MCP
entries.what: Drives a real browser: opens pages, clicks, types, fills forms, uploads files, runs page scripts, takes screenshots and saves PDFs. It can clear cookies and stored site data.
entries.riskNote: It acts as whoever is signed in on any site the browser opens. The yes and no answers do not show that.

manual: Needs Node, for npx.
By hand in Claude Code: claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest
By hand in Codex: codex mcp add playwright npx "@playwright/mcp@latest"

entries.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
entries.what: Controls and inspects a live Chrome: input, navigation, network and console, performance traces, Lighthouse audits, heap snapshots, and installing or removing extensions.
entries.riskNote: It acts as whoever is signed in on any site the browser opens. The yes and no answers do not show that.

manual: Needs a current Node and a current Chrome.
By hand: add a server to your client with the command npx and the arguments -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest
In Claude Code that is: claude mcp add chrome-devtools -- npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest
Google collects usage statistics unless the server is started with --no-usage-statistics. The app starts it with that flag.

entries.name: Serena
entries.what: Finds and edits code by symbol through language servers, with refactoring that includes safe delete, a file search and replace, project memory, and a tool that runs shell commands.

manual: The maker says not to install Serena through an MCP or plugin marketplace, so there is no install button. Follow its own quick start.
Install uv first.
uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent
serena init
Claude Code: claude mcp add --scope user serena -- serena start-mcp-server --context claude-code --project-from-cwd
Codex: add [mcp_servers.serena] to ~/.codex/config.toml with command = "serena" and args = ["start-mcp-server", "--project-from-cwd", "--context=codex"]

entries.name: Sentry MCP
entries.what: Searches errors, traces and logs, reads issues, events, releases and docs, and creates or deletes projects, teams, keys, alert rules and monitors. Hosted by Sentry.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http sentry --scope user https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp
Then sign in: run /mcp in a Claude Code session and pick the server, or run claude mcp login sentry in a terminal. A browser opens.
Or the maker's plugin: claude plugin marketplace add getsentry/sentry-mcp, then claude plugin install sentry-mcp@sentry-mcp
Codex: the maker gives no line. Codex's own way for a hosted server is to add [mcp_servers.sentry] with url = "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp" to ~/.codex/config.toml, then run codex mcp login sentry
Self hosted Sentry: the maker has a local mode, npx @sentry/mcp-server@latest with an access token, and calls it a work in progress.

entries.name: Linear MCP
entries.what: Finds, creates and updates issues, projects, comments and other objects in Linear. Hosted by Linear. A read only address exists.
entries.riskNote: Linear's page prints no tool list, only that tools find, create and update. Sends, spends and deletes were not confirmed.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http linear-server --scope user https://mcp.linear.app/mcp
Then sign in: run /mcp in a Claude Code session and pick the server, or run claude mcp login linear-server in a terminal. A browser opens.
Codex: codex mcp add linear --url https://mcp.linear.app/mcp, then codex mcp login linear
Read only: use the address https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly instead.
A Linear API key or OAuth token can be sent as a bearer header instead of signing in.

entries.name: Atlassian MCP Server
entries.what: Reads, searches and writes Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Loom, Goals, Projects, Teams and Compass. Jira delete and manage tool groups exist and stay off until an admin turns them on.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http atlassian --scope user https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp
Then sign in: run /mcp in a Claude Code session and pick the server, or run claude mcp login atlassian in a terminal. A browser opens.
Codex: codex mcp add atlassian --url https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp
An API token works for a setup with no browser, unless the organisation admin has switched token sign in off.
The old SSE address stopped on 30 June 2026. Use the address above.

entries.name: Notion MCP
entries.what: Searches and reads a Notion workspace, creates, updates, moves and duplicates pages and databases, adds comments, and moves pages and databases to Trash. Hosted by Notion.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http notion --scope user https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
Then sign in: run /mcp in a Claude Code session and pick the server, or run claude mcp login notion in a terminal. A browser opens.
Codex: add [mcp_servers.notion] with url = "https://mcp.notion.com/mcp" to ~/.codex/config.toml, then run codex mcp login notion
Sign in through the browser is the only way in. There is no key setup for the hosted server.
Notion also has a Claude Code plugin with skills and commands: github.com/makenotion/claude-code-notion-plugin

entries.name: Slack MCP server
entries.what: Slack's hosted server: searches messages, files, users and channels, reads channels and threads, sends and schedules messages, adds reactions, and creates and updates canvases. For Claude Code it comes inside Slack's plugin.
entries.licence: MIT (slackapi/slack-skills-plugin, the plugin that connects to the server)

steps.label: Add Anthropic's official plugin list (no change if it is there)
Install the plugin for your user

manual: Claude Code, in a session: /plugin install slack@claude-plugins-official
The same from a terminal: claude plugin install slack@claude-plugins-official
The plugin sets up the server at https://mcp.slack.com/mcp and adds Slack skills. You sign in to your workspace in the browser the first time it is used.
A workspace admin may have to approve the app first.
Adding the address alone is not enough: Slack has no dynamic client registration and only admits registered apps. The plugin carries Slack's own client.
Codex: codex plugin marketplace add slackapi/slack-skills-plugin, then codex plugin add slack@slack. That gives the skills only; the server is not wired into Codex yet.

entries.name: Supabase MCP
entries.what: Lists and queries a Supabase project, runs SQL and migrations, deploys edge functions, manages branches and storage settings, and can create, pause and restore projects. A read only switch and a single project scope are set in the address.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http supabase --scope user https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp
Then sign in: run /mcp in a Claude Code session and pick the server, or run claude mcp login supabase in a terminal. A browser opens.
Supabase's own page builds a line for one project, with --scope project and a features list in the address. Use that to keep it to one project.
Safer: add read_only=true and project_ref with your project to the address, as the README shows.

Codex: the maker gives no line. Codex's own way for a hosted server is to add [mcp_servers.supabase] with url = "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp" to ~/.codex/config.toml, then run codex mcp login supabase
It asks before create_project and create_branch, which cost money, when the client can show the question.

entries.name: Figma MCP server
entries.what: Reads design context, variables, screenshots and Code Connect maps from Figma files. The hosted server also writes to the canvas: use_figma creates, edits and deletes objects, and image generation uses Figma AI credits.
entries.licence: No licence file in the repository

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: Claude Code, the server alone: claude mcp add --transport http figma --scope user https://mcp.figma.com/mcp
Then sign in: run /mcp in a Claude Code session and pick the server, or run claude mcp login figma in a terminal. A browser opens.
Figma recommends its plugin, which adds skills as well: claude plugin install figma@claude-plugins-official
Gemini CLI: gemini extensions install https://github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide
Read limits depend on your Figma seat and plan. Starter plans and View or Collab seats get up to 6 tool calls a month.

entries.name: Stripe MCP
entries.what: Reads and writes the Stripe API: customers, invoices, subscriptions, refunds, payment links and more, plus Treasury tools that send and transfer money. One tool can call any write method of the API.
entries.riskNote: stripe_api_write reaches any POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE method, so it can charge, refund, delete and send invoices to customers.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http stripe --scope user https://mcp.stripe.com
Then sign in: run /mcp in a Claude Code session and pick the server, or run claude mcp login stripe in a terminal. A browser opens. You choose live or sandbox accounts and the permissions for each.
Codex: codex mcp add stripe --url https://mcp.stripe.com
Where sign in is not possible, the only other way is a Stripe agent API key sent as a bearer header and kept in an environment variable.
From 31 October 2026 Stripe rejects full access secret keys and restricted keys without the Agent tag.
Turn on your client's tool approval so each call is reviewed before it runs. Stripe asks for that.
Stripe's own setup command, which also installs its skills: stripe agent setup

entries.name: Vercel MCP
entries.what: Reads projects, deployments, logs and analytics, creates and cancels deployments, edits projects, domains and environment variables, and can buy domains, credits, add ons and the Pro plan.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http vercel --scope user https://mcp.vercel.com
Then sign in: run /mcp in a Claude Code session and pick the server, or run claude mcp login vercel in a terminal. A browser opens.
Codex: codex mcp add vercel --url https://mcp.vercel.com
Vercel only admits clients it has reviewed and approved. Claude Code and Codex CLI are on its list.
It has purchase tools. Read the tools page before an agent uses it alone.

entries.name: Cloudflare API MCP Server
entries.what: Three tools cover the whole Cloudflare API, about 2,500 endpoints: search the docs, search the API description, and run code that calls any endpoint. What it may change is set by the permissions chosen at sign in.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: The README gives the address and no line for a named client. In Claude Code that is: claude mcp add --transport http cloudflare-api --scope user https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp
Then sign in: run /mcp in a Claude Code session and pick the server, or run claude mcp login cloudflare-api in a terminal. A browser opens. You pick the permissions there.
Without a browser: create a Cloudflare API token with the permissions you need and send it as a bearer header.

Codex: the maker gives no line. Codex's own way for a hosted server is to add [mcp_servers.cloudflare-api] with url = "https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp" to ~/.codex/config.toml, then run codex mcp login cloudflare-api
Cloudflare calls this its recommended server and lists some of its older single product servers as deprecated.

entries.name: AWS MCP Server
entries.what: AWS's managed server: makes any authenticated AWS API call, runs scripts in a sandbox, and searches and reads AWS documentation. It can do whatever the signed in identity is allowed to do.
entries.pinned: aws/mcp-proxy-for-aws v1.7.0 (the optional local proxy; the hosted server has no version)
entries.riskNote: Any AWS API call includes creating paid resources, deleting them, and sending mail or text messages through AWS services.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: First attach the managed policy AWSMCPSignInOAuthAccessPolicy to your IAM role or user.
Claude Code: claude mcp add aws-mcp https://aws-mcp.us-east-1.api.aws/mcp --transport http
The first tool call opens AWS sign in in the browser. Tokens last 1 hour and renew for up to 12.
Another Region: swap us-east-1 in the address. The page lists eight.
Codex: codex mcp add aws-mcp --url https://aws-mcp.us-east-1.api.aws/mcp?oauth=initialize

For several accounts, a default Region or a read only mode, AWS points to its local proxy instead: aws login, then the server command uvx mcp-proxy-for-aws-cli@latest https://aws-mcp.us-east-1.api.aws/mcp --metadata AWS_REGION=us-west-2
The proxy takes --read-only to hide the tools that may write.

entries.name: Terraform MCP Server
entries.what: Looks up providers, modules and policies in the Terraform Registry with no sign in. With a token and the terraform tool group it reads and changes HCP Terraform workspaces, variables and runs, including plan, apply and a safe workspace delete.
entries.riskNote: The app starts it with no token and only the registry tools, which read. The label is for the whole server, as it is with a token.

manual: Needs Docker, installed and running.
By hand in Claude Code: claude mcp add terraform -s user -t stdio -- docker run -i --rm hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server
By hand in Codex: codex mcp add terraform -- docker run -i --rm hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server
For HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise add TFE_ADDRESS and TFE_TOKEN to the docker line and choose the tool groups with --toolsets. The app does neither.
Tools that need approval stay off unless ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS is set.

entries.name: Semgrep MCP server
entries.what: Scans code for security problems, runs custom rules and supply chain scans, and reads findings from the Semgrep platform when a token is set. For Claude Code it comes as the Semgrep Guardian plugin: the server, hooks that scan what an agent writes, and skills.
entries.licence: LGPL-2.1 (semgrep/semgrep). The plugin repository has no licence file.
entries.riskNote: The plugin adds hooks that run before and after every file write and shell command, and a setup skill that installs the Semgrep program.

steps.label: Add Anthropic's official plugin list (no change if it is there)
Install the plugin for your user

manual: Claude Code, as the README says: open /plugin, go to Discover, search for Semgrep and install it.
The same from a terminal: claude plugin install semgrep@claude-plugins-official
Then run /setup-semgrep-plugin in a session. It also installs the Semgrep program.
Other clients: brew install semgrep, then add a server with the command semgrep and the argument mcp
With Docker: docker run -i --rm semgrep/semgrep semgrep mcp -t stdio
Optional: set SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN to connect to Semgrep AppSec Platform.

entries.name: PostHog MCP
entries.what: Reads and writes across PostHog: analytics queries and SQL, feature flags, experiments, dashboards, error tracking, data pipelines and support tickets. Hundreds of tools, with many delete tools, ticket replies and broadcasts.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

manual: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http posthog https://mcp.posthog.com/mcp -s user
The first use asks you to log in to PostHog. It routes you to the US or EU region by your account.
Codex: codex mcp add posthog --url https://mcp.posthog.com/mcp
PostHog's own installer for several clients: npx @posthog/wizard mcp add
Some tools use models inside PostHog and may be billed as PostHog AI spend.

entries.name: HubSpot MCP server
entries.what: Searches and reads CRM records, conversations, owners and reports, and creates or updates CRM records, campaigns, marketing email drafts, segments and properties. It can create, edit and publish landing pages, site pages and blog posts.
entries.riskNote: Publishing a landing page, site page or blog post puts content in front of people, so it counts as sending.

manual: In your HubSpot account open MCP Connectors and click Create MCP connector. Give it a name and a redirect URL.
Keep the connector's client ID and client secret.
Server address: https://mcp.hubspot.com over streamable HTTP. Sign in is OAuth with PKCE through your connector.
HubSpot's page gives no command for Claude Code or Codex, so there is no install button.
Claude Code's own way for a server with a fixed client: claude mcp add --transport http --client-id with your client ID, --client-secret and --callback-port, then the name and the address.
With that way the connector's redirect URL is http://localhost:PORT/callback, with the port you gave.
After connecting, run get_user_details to see which tools your account has.

entries.name: Intercom MCP server
entries.what: Searches and reads Intercom conversations, contacts, companies and Help Center articles, adds internal notes to conversations, and creates and updates articles, which it can publish. 14 tools. US and EU workspaces.
entries.licence: No licence file in the repository
entries.pinned: 96140be28cf8eeb2ae4a4c860ca1eddcdfb006d9 (repository head; the tool list was read from developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/mcp)
entries.riskNote: create_article and update_article can set an article to published, which puts it in the Help Center. Internal notes go to teammates only.

steps.label: Add the server to Claude Code, for every project

entries.name: Superpowers
entries.what: A development method as 15 skills (brainstorm, plan, test first, review, git worktrees) with a session start hook that loads it into every session. Ships shell and JavaScript files.
entries.pinned: 5bf4e78011075bcfc0dc295f0724994cd123ee71 (the commit the official list installs; release v7.0.0 is newer)

steps.label: Add Anthropic's official plugin list (no change if it is there)
Install the plugin for your user

manual: In a Claude Code session: /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official
The same from a terminal: claude plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official
On a machine where Claude Code has never been opened, first run: claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official
It loads the next time Claude Code starts, or after /reload-plugins
Codex CLI: open /plugins and search for superpowers
Gemini CLI: gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
Copilot CLI: copilot plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace, then copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

entries.name: GitHub CLI (gh)
entries.what: GitHub from the terminal: pull requests, issues, releases, workflow runs, secrets, gists, codespaces and raw API calls. Its repo commands include create, archive and delete.

steps.label: Install the GitHub CLI with Homebrew

manual: macOS or Linux with Homebrew, the way its maintainers recommend: brew install gh
Windows: WinGet, or a download from the releases page. The README links both.
Then sign in: gh auth login. A browser opens. A token in GH_TOKEN works too.

entries.name: ripgrep (rg)
entries.what: Searches files under a folder for a pattern, fast, and respects ignore files. It only reads.

steps.label: Install ripgrep with Homebrew

manual: macOS or Linux with Homebrew: brew install ripgrep
With Rust: cargo install ripgrep
Windows: winget install BurntSushi.ripgrep.MSVC
The command it adds is rg.

entries.name: jq
entries.what: Filters and reshapes JSON on the command line. It reads its input and prints the result.

steps.label: Install jq with Homebrew

manual: macOS with Homebrew: brew install jq
Debian and Ubuntu: sudo apt-get install jq
Windows: winget install jqlang.jq
Or download a release from https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases

entries.name: uv
entries.what: Python package and project manager. Installs Python versions, packages and tools, makes environments, and runs tools straight from the package index with uvx. Many MCP servers start through it.

steps.label: Install uv with Homebrew

manual: With Homebrew: brew install uv
From PyPI: pipx install uv, or pip install uv
Windows: winget install --id=astral-sh.uv -e
Astral's own installer is a script piped into a shell. The app never runs one. The README has it if you want it.

entries.name: Node.js
entries.what: JavaScript runtime. Agents and MCP servers installed with npm or started with npx need it. It runs whatever script it is handed.
entries.riskNote: A runtime has no tool list to read. It can do whatever the script it runs can do.

manual: Download the installer for your system from https://nodejs.org/en/download/ and run it.
The README gives that download page and no command, so there is no install button.
Check it: node --version

entries.name: Bun
entries.what: JavaScript runtime, package manager, bundler and test runner in one program. Adds and removes packages, runs scripts, publishes packages, and runs tools with bunx.
entries.licence: MIT (bundled parts carry their own licences)

steps.label: Install Bun with npm

manual: With npm: npm install -g bun
With Homebrew: brew tap oven-sh/bun, then brew install bun
Oven's own installer is a script piped into a shell. The app never runs one. The README has it if you want it.

entries.name: Docker
entries.what: Builds, pulls, pushes, runs and removes containers and images. Several servers in this list start as a docker run command.
entries.licence: Apache-2.0 (docker/cli). Docker Desktop has its own terms.

manual: Download Docker Desktop for your system from https://docs.docker.com/get-started/get-docker/ and install it.
Docker gives that download page and no command, so there is no install button.

Docker Desktop is free for personal use, education, open source that is not commercial, and small businesses: fewer than 250 employees and less than 10 million US dollars a year. Otherwise it needs a paid subscription.
Start Docker before you start an agent that uses a server in a container.

entries.name: ccusage
entries.what: Reads the session logs coding agents keep on the machine and reports token use and cost by day, week, month and session.

manual: Nothing to install: the README says to run it straight from the package runner.
In a terminal: npx ccusage@latest
With Bun: bunx ccusage
A report by day, week, month or session: add daily, weekly, monthly or session.

entries.name: ccstatusline
entries.what: A status line for Claude Code that is set up in a terminal menu: model, git branch, token and context use, with themes. It keeps its settings in ~/.config/ccstatusline/settings.json.

manual: Its setup is a menu in the terminal, so the app cannot run it for you.
In a terminal: npx -y ccstatusline@latest
With Bun: bunx -y ccstatusline@latest
In the menu choose the option that installs it to Claude Code settings.
Choose Pinned global install in the first setup if Claude Code should stay on one version and not follow the newest.

entries.name: Repomix
entries.what: Packs a whole repository, local or a remote one given by address, into a single file an agent can read.

steps.label: Install Repomix with npm

manual: With npm: npm install -g repomix
With Homebrew: brew install repomix
Then run repomix inside a project folder. It writes one file that holds the repository.
One try with no install: npx repomix@latest, run inside the project folder. It packs the folder it is run in.
Claude Code plugins: /plugin marketplace add yamadashy/repomix, then /plugin install repomix-mcp@repomix

entries.name: Spec Kit
entries.what: Sets up spec driven development in a project: after install, specify init writes commands, templates and scripts for the chosen agent, then the agent works from spec to plan to tasks.

steps.label: Install the Specify CLI with uv

manual: Needs Python 3.11 or later and uv.
From PyPI, one of its two official channels: uv tool install specify-cli
Or with pipx: pipx install specify-cli
The route its maintainers recommend installs from the repository at a release tag: uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git@v1.2.0
Then, in a terminal: specify init my-project --integration copilot
Swap copilot for your agent. The README lists the ones it supports.
Check it: specify version

entries.name: CC Safety Net
entries.what: A guard that reads each command or file access before the agent runs it and blocks destructive ones (for example rm -rf and hard git resets) and reads of secrets such as SSH keys and .env files. Its installer writes the hook into the agent's settings.
entries.riskNote: The install step runs the newest release, not a pinned one: the maker asks for @latest so an older cached copy is not used.

steps.label: Install the guard into Claude Code

manual: Needs Node 18 or later.
Claude Code: npx -y cc-safety-net@latest install --claude-code
Other agents take their own flag, one per run: --codex, --gemini-cli, --copilot-cli, --opencode, --cursor
Check that it works: npx -y cc-safety-net@latest doctor
With no flag the installer opens a menu, so run that form in a terminal yourself.
Remove it: npx -y cc-safety-net@latest uninstall --claude-code
